html:
The Winefelly were a band of the Kalapuya people in the upper Willamette Valley of Oregon, near today's Eugene and Springfield. Like other Kalapuya bands they burned the valley grasslands to keep them open, gathered camas bulbs and acorns, and hunted deer.

Little is written about this band alone. Malaria in the 1830s killed most Kalapuya, and settlers on the Oregon Trail took the valley in the 1840s. In treaties of 1855 the bands gave up the valley and were moved to the Grand Ronde reservation, now the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde. Neighbours: Chelamela and Santiam.
